question: Using elementary row operations, transform $$A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&3\\2&5&8\\1&3&5\end{bmatrix}$$ into $$B=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&3\\0&1&2\\0&0&0\end{bmatrix},$$ and then demonstrate the reversibility of the elementary operations by applying an appropriate reverse sequence to $B$ to recover $A$.
explanation:
Transformation of $A$ into $B$

Starting with $$A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&3\\2&5&8\\1&3&5\end{bmatrix},$$ apply $R_2\to R_2-2R_1$. This gives $$\begin{bmatrix}1&2&3\\0&1&2\\1&3&5\end{bmatrix}$$ Now apply $R_3\to R_3-R_1$, obtaining $$\begin{bmatrix}1&2&3\\0&1&2\\0&1&2\end{bmatrix}$$ Applying $R_3\to R_3-R_2$, we get $$\begin{bmatrix}1&2&3\\0&1&2\\0&0&0\end{bmatrix}=B$$

Reversing the Operations

To recover $A$, apply the inverse elementary operations in reverse order. Starting from $B$, apply $R_3\to R_3+R_2$ to obtain $$\begin{bmatrix}1&2&3\\0&1&2\\0&1&2\end{bmatrix}$$ Then apply $R_3\to R_3+R_1$, giving $$\begin{bmatrix}1&2&3\\0&1&2\\1&3&5\end{bmatrix}$$ Finally, apply $R_2\to R_2+2R_1$. Thus, $$\begin{bmatrix}1&2&3\\2&5&8\\1&3&5\end{bmatrix}=A$$ Hence, the stated elementary row operations transform $A$ into $B$, and reversing them recovers the original matrix.

options.A: $R_2\to R_2-2R_1$, $R_3\to R_3-R_1$, $R_3\to R_3-R_2$ transform $A$ to $B$; reversing with $R_3\to R_3+R_2$, $R_3\to R_3+R_1$, $R_2\to R_2+2R_1$ recovers $A$
